newsitem.title: UK: Britain protests as French strike strands truckers.
newsitem.headline: Britain protests as French strike strands truckers.

text.p: Britain has called for an end to a week-long strike by French lorry drivers that has stranded hundreds of British trucks and could cause severe financial damage to small operators.
Secretary of State for Transport George Young voiced concern about the plight of British drivers in a letter to his French counterpart Bernard Pons at the weekend, officials said on Monday.
"Hundreds of British hauliers remain stranded in various parts of France," Young said. "I naturally hope that this action can be brought to an end as soon as possible."
Young said some British drivers had been stranded for six days and there would be many claims for compensation for damage to perishable cargoes and for loss of earnings.
"This dispute is causing particularly severe problems for small operators, some of whom may be unable to sustain the losses they are incurring," he said.

Britain's Road Haulage Association said more than 700 British vehicles were estimated to have been caught up in the blockade by French drivers seeking higher wages, shorter hours and earlier retirement.

"This is a combination of industrial anarchy and official incompetence," said Sydney Balgarnie, a spokesman for the industry group. "There are drivers who have been trapped for some days and they are running out of money and food."
The British truckers want the French authorities to provide certificates to substantiate any claims for compensation.
The British Foreign Office has advised people not to travel to France with trucks but it is difficult to find alternative routes especially to reach Spain and Portugal.
The French truckers reinforced their campaign on Monday, with barricades at five frontier posts with Germany and blockades at the ports of Calais and Boulogne -- major routes for ferries to Britain.
The problems for British drivers have been exacerbated by the closure of the Channel Tunnel last week because of a fire. The tunnel has been reopened to freight trains only.
